title: Projected cost bound for partial runs
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $0<\tau\le1$ be a rational threshold. Suppose $P$ maps learning costs to natural numbers, satisfies $P(0)=0$ and $P(c+d)=P(c)+P(d)$ for all costs $c,d$, and let $B$ be a natural number such that, for every $k<n$, every active family of subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and every supported outcome of the corresponding stage-estimation program, the projected cost is at most $B$ times the number of candidates in that stage. Then for every $k\le n$, every supported outcome of the algorithm run through $k$ stages has projected cost at most $k\bigl(P(16(n+1)^2(\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil+1)^2)+2\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil B\bigr)$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
The projection $P$ is additive on pairs of learning costs
The stage-cost bound holds for every $k<n$, every active family, and every supported stage outcome
The outcome is supported by the run distribution through $k$ stages
